text:
Phillip Danault came home to Montreal last season, and this year he's a pending free agent, the subject of columns arguing the Canadiens should extend him. With Chris Kreider out, he's also playing more, up to about 20 minutes a night from 17.

His results look poor and his process looks good. Montreal takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than 8 points better than without him, and his own chances are up to 0.70 expected goals per 60 from 0.54. He has 2 goals on 4.0 expected, so the finishing has let him down. Our wins added ranks him near the bottom of the league, but that measures goals, and the goals haven't come.

He's always been valued for the defensive work, and our model compares him to Sean Couturier and Adam Lowry. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, which is why the contract question isn't simple. Our talent range has him around 12 goals. At 33, he's still one of the forwards Montreal trusts most when it needs to defend a lead.
